newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices hold, helped by crude, gas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices hold, helped by crude, gas.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices held relatively steady Friday in sluggish activity, helped by firmer crude and natural gas markets though mild East Coast weather still tempted the bears, traders said.

"If crude holds at $20-plus, I think resid could move up, but there's nothing significant happening on the weather front next week and that means there's not going to be a lot of demand," said one cash trader, noting firmer city gate gas prices this week also helped make resid more competitive.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was unchanged at $15.75-16.00 a barrel, with August one percent paper also flat at about $16.00-20.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour still seemed well supported, inching up slightly to $17.50-75 on reports a New York utility's buy program for August would tally about 850,000 barrels, traders said.
High sulphurs in New York mostly held steady, with 2.2 percent still quoted at $14.75-15.00.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices were stable, with three percent still at $14.50-75 though some thought the value was higher.
USG one percent was still at $15.50-75.
A trader said 60,000 barrels of prompt USG two percent (high viscosity) sold at $14.05 (FOB Houston), but the deal could not be confirmed.

New York city gate gas prices edged up a couple of cents Friday to the mid-$2.40s/mmBtu, or $15.44 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, firmed slightly to $2.23/mmBtu, or $14.05 a barrel.
